name: Novi
pitch: Local AI desktop agent for Windows: voice control, screen understanding, parallel workers.
description: A voice assistant that lives on the Windows desktop as an animated pixel-art robot and carries out spoken requests on the PC: music, live weather and travel times, notes, PowerPoint decks, explaining anything snipped from the screen, and taught routines. All models run locally through Ollama.

hardestProblem: Getting a small local 3B model to drive a real desktop reliably and safely: deterministic fast paths for common intents, agent loop guards and completion nudges, UI Automation by control name, and document-state safety checks.
results: About 3x model throughput for 4 simultaneous calls after enabling Ollama parallelism (2.3 s vs 1.8 s for one call; informal measurement, RTX 3050 6 GB)
Two-city weather comparison with two parallel workers answered in 4-6 s (informal measurement)
Scripted self-recorded demo: 13 scenes, all successful in one take

highlights: Built a fully local Windows voice agent in Python (faster-whisper, Ollama with qwen2.5 3B models) that controls apps, media, PowerPoint and the browser from natural-language requests on a 6 GB laptop GPU.

Designed a coordinator that splits goals across up to 4 parallel workers, each with its own headless Playwright browser, with a shared screen lock for desktop actions; about 3x throughput for 4 simultaneous model calls after enabling Ollama parallelism.
Implemented snip-to-ask screen Q&A combining Windows OCR with a local vision model (qwen2.5vl), including follow-up questions.
Added persistent SQLite memory and teachable workflows (spoken instructions or recorded demonstration, replayed via UI Automation by control name) with an in-app editor.
Improved reliability of a small local model with deterministic fast paths, loop guards and document-safety checks, covered by 63 offline pytest tests.
Built an animated pixel-art desktop character, worker sprites and task panel in Tkinter on an event bus, plus a self-recording scripted demo.
